ranked.headline: Predicted structures now guide design of antibodies, peptides, TCRs and aptamers
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple structure predictors and generative models with epitope, kinetic, and biophysical objectives for binder design.

ranked.headline: External ground truth now anchors evaluation of drug response and genomics methods
ranked.summary: Recent preprints supply leakage-audited, evolutionary, and calibrated reference standards to test predictive methods beyond in-sample fit.

ranked.headline: Deep and mechanistic models integrate multimodal single-cell and spatial data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend single-cell modeling toward multimodal, spatial and dynamical settings, with explicit relational structure encoded in the models.

ranked.headline: ML classifiers and bias-aware models refine sequence-derived measurements
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers apply ML and bias-modeling to correct technical distortion in sequencing and amplification data before biological inference.

ranked.headline: Learned models judged on conditioned tasks like epitope ranking and binding affinity
ranked.summary: Preprints test learned models on task-specific conditions such as epitope-conditioned ranking, novel-compound generalization, and calibrated uncertainty.

ranked.headline: Deep models fuse biological priors and topology into omics representation learning
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers embed gene-regulatory, LLM-derived and topological priors into deep models for omics and pathology data.

ranked.headline: Population geometry and drift statistics test mechanisms of neural dynamics
ranked.summary: Population geometry and representational drift statistics are now used as criteria for judging candidate neural mechanisms.

ranked.headline: Learned and coarse-grained models generate and validate protein conformational ensembles
ranked.summary: Learned and enhanced-sampling methods are now being tested against benchmarks for multi-state protein sampling in biological contexts.

ranked.headline: Local structural states and their couplings govern protein function and dysfunction
ranked.summary: Recent work quantifies allosteric, topological, and salt-bridge couplings that determine protein function beyond static structure.

ranked.headline: Deep learning advances peptide identification and protein function annotation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints add benchmarks, training-free inference and repository-scale search to machine learning tools for peptide and protein annotation.

ranked.headline: MD simulations resolve dynamic drug binding and viral envelope assembly at membranes
ranked.summary: Current simulation studies apply atomistic and coarse-grained MD to membranes, viral assembly, and cryo-EM density interpretation.

ranked.headline: Sequence-level readouts reveal context-dependent function across editing and design
ranked.summary: Deep sequencing, covariation models, and generative ML now score individual sequence variants directly, exposing context-dependent functional outcomes.

ranked.headline: Graph and topological metrics quantify spatial organization in tissue and glycan data
ranked.summary: Invariant and graph-based descriptors now expose spatial complexity in simulated tumours, multispecies tissue states, and N-glycan patterns.

ranked.headline: Lineage-tree methods infer single-cell fate and proliferation dynamics
ranked.summary: Sequential CRISPR lineage recordings and single-cell transcriptomes now support joint inference of lineage trees and fate or proliferation dynamics.

ranked.headline: Learned models predict molecular encodings, antimicrobial synergy, and hepatotoxicity
ranked.summary: Learned predictors now target combination effects and mechanistic readouts, not only property endpoints, at the modeling stage.

ranked.headline: Cortical topography as a constraint and intermediate representation in brain models
ranked.summary: Preprints now use cortical topography maps as constraints and intermediates for functional region discovery, connectome mapping, and recurrent network design.

ranked.headline: Sparse and mechanistic interpretability methods probe generative protein models
ranked.summary: Generative protein and antibody models are being examined mechanistically and steered toward diverse, structurally plausible outputs.

ranked.headline: New computational methods for genome assembly, population genetics and phylogenomics
ranked.summary: Sequence-based evolutionary inference tools are advancing across assembly benchmarking, reference-free population genomics, and orthology and selection analysis.

ranked.headline: Statistical models add annotations, covariates and time to GWAS-based genomic prediction
ranked.summary: Summary-statistic and cohort methods now encode annotations, covariates and time directly into genomic prediction models.

ranked.headline: Haplotype and structural variant inference from imputed or low-depth genotype data
ranked.summary: Imputed and low-depth data are now serving as the basis for haplotype, structural, and kinship inference without deep sequencing.

ranked.headline: Computational methods assign cell identity and quality-check pooled single-cell data
ranked.summary: Large integrated atlases and new annotation tools make cell identity assignment, unknown-type handling, and pooled-sample QC central.

ranked.headline: Inferring RNA-mediated regulation from interaction, network, and composition data
ranked.summary: Recent methods extend RNA regulatory inference from interaction calling toward fate decisions, enhancer activity, and speckle localization.

ranked.headline: Protein language models encode nativeness, taxonomy, and memorization beyond training
ranked.summary: Diagnostic probes now test what protein language models learn beyond benchmark accuracy, from sequence origin to memorization.

ranked.headline: Integrative models resolve chromatin states, enhancers, and Tn5 bias in epigenomes
ranked.summary: Explainable AI nominates H3K18ac as an enhancer mark, while IHEC-scale models extend chromatin state annotation across 1,698 epigenomes.

ranked.headline: Curvature-derived geometry and dual virtual nodes target protein-ligand binding affinity
ranked.summary: Three June 2026 items encode binding geometry via curvature and virtual-node fusion for affinity prediction, with no pretraining described in their summaries.

ranked.headline: Mass spectrometry workflows move from protein to proteoform-level differential analysis
ranked.summary: Recent published workflows pair peptide-level differential statistics with intact-protein characterization to resolve proteoforms.

ranked.headline: Biology agents are scored on checkable tasks, grounded in tools and structured evidence
ranked.summary: Benchmarks like EpiBench and ABC-Bench now measure agent performance on defined, verifiable biological tasks rather than open-ended prompting.

ranked.headline: Simulations map gating and allosteric transitions in transporters and signalling proteins
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study pair multi-scale and Markov state simulations with cryo-EM to resolve pathway- and gating-level transitions.

ranked.headline: Evaluation metric reverses drug-response model rankings under held-out chemistry
ranked.summary: Foundation-model and physics-informed predictors for drug response and pharmacokinetics are being judged by leakage, metric choice, and identifiability.

ranked.headline: Software for reproducible omics analysis across transcriptomic and spatial modalities
ranked.summary: Reference-free and module-level evaluation is entering omics software, addressing benchmarking where ground truth is unavailable.

ranked.headline: Genome comparisons link structural change to plant arid and altitude adaptation
ranked.summary: Chromosome-scale assemblies and k-mer methods now enable structure-resolved comparisons across plant lineages and polyploid pangenomes.

ranked.headline: Bayesian models capture uncertainty in mutational signatures and miRNA target prediction
ranked.summary: Explicit probabilistic structure is being applied to mutational signatures, miRNA targeting, and spatial proteomic survival modeling.

ranked.headline: Faster read alignment and tandem repeat genotyping for population sequencing
ranked.summary: Recent tools speed short-read alignment and scale tandem repeat genotyping and immunoglobulin chain reconstruction from sequencing data.

ranked.headline: Interneuron connectivity and M-current shape oscillation regimes in network models
ranked.summary: Reduced models now link gamma and multistable oscillations to interneuron class connectivity and intrinsic excitability.

ranked.headline: Separating noise from growth dynamics in single-cell and time-series models
ranked.summary: Five preprints from June 2026 pair interpretable or likelihood-based models with noise-aware inference of dynamics from time-series and single-cell data.

ranked.headline: Computational models link viral host interactions and bacterial resistance evolution
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a publication apply metabolic, protein-interaction, and phylogenetic inference to pathogen phenotypes and host dependencies.

ranked.headline: Gene loss, germline hypermutability and introgression shape functional genetic variation
ranked.summary: Comparative and population genomic studies now treat gene loss, germline hypermutability and archaic introgression as units of variation.

ranked.headline: Harmonized metadata and automated workflows make microscopy and scRNA-seq data reusable
ranked.summary: Growing multi-source imaging and single-cell archives require explicit, harmonized metadata to make data reusable at national and consortium scale.

ranked.headline: Alignment-free k-mer and distribution methods infer and score human centromere structure
ranked.summary: T2T assemblies make centromeres assessable, and new alignment-free metrics target centromere scoring and length inference from short reads.

ranked.headline: Domain architecture and tree constraints reshape orthogroup inference in complex genomes
ranked.summary: New orthology methods benchmark against OrthoFinder and constrain candidate groups beyond global sequence comparison.
